previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old male with a history of acute myeloid leukemia in remission following allogeneic stem cell transplant and extensive chronic graft-versus-host disease was admitted for worsening bilateral foot and leg pain with ulcerations and malodorous skin sloughing. He had been experiencing increasing pain for several weeks and was concerned about infection. Evaluation by infectious disease and wound care found no evidence of active infection, and the wounds appeared improved from two weeks prior. Pain management was optimized with the addition of gabapentin and tramadol to his existing oxycodone regimen, resulting in significant improvement. He continued his baseline immunosuppressive and prophylactic medications, including ciprofloxacin and amoxicillin for pseudomonas prevention, and received IVIG for hypogammaglobulinemia. He was discharged home with new wound care instructions and a plan to follow up with his hematologist and wound care clinic.
